articles.title: Bioelectrical and optogenetic modulation for neuroimmune therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Neuroimmune interactions are emerging as key regulators of inflammation, immunity, immune homeostasis, and disease progression. Neural circuits do not merely sense tissue injury, but also actively shape immune-cell recruitment, cytokine production, vascular function, and organ-level inflammatory outcomes. Here, we overview bioelectrical and optogenetic systems for neuroimmune modulation in diseases via the defined neural and inflammatory pathway. First, we review systemic neuroimmune modulating pathway and local neuroimmune modulators, and identify established neuroimmune molecular interactions in diseases. After that, we explain bioelectrical and optogenetic systems employed to modulate neuroimmune interactions. We evaluate representative studies with advanced delivery systems in consideration of neural target, immune effector, disease-relevant outcome, and safety. Finally, this review highlights both positive and negative clinical evidence of electroceuticals, and ultrasound-mediated and optogenetic systems predominantly in preclinical development. In summary and perspective, we prioritize and discuss the requirements for their further clinical translation. The integration of neural targeting with advanced materials and adaptive gene and drug delivery would be successfully harnessed for programmable therapies to modulate disease-relevant immune circuits without broadly suppressing host defense systems.

articles.title: Ubiquitination of retinoic acid receptor alpha promotes severe acute pancreatitis-associated acute lung injury by releasing hexokinase 3 transcriptional repression.
articles.abstract: Lung macrophages constitute the first line of defense against environmental attack and participate in the pathogenesis of acute lung injury (ALI). In this study, we sought to elucidate the impact of HK3 on the regulation of macrophage phenotype in severe acute pancreatitis (SAP)-associated acute lung injury (PALI). HK3 expression was enhanced in lung macrophages of mice with SAP, and overexpression of HK3 in macrophages using adeno-associated viral vectors exacerbated PALI progression and increased macrophage M1 polarization in lung tissues. Overexpression of HK3 enhanced the glycolytic activity of macrophages, thereby polarizing macrophages toward the M1 phenotype. Retinoic acid receptor alpha (RARA) repressed HK3 transcription by binding to the promoter of HK3. Knockdown of HK3 inhibited the macrophage glycolysis induced by RARA knockdown and alleviated PALI development. NEDD4L mediated ubiquitination and degradation of RARA, and NEDD4L overexpression promoted macrophage glycolysis-induced increase in M1 polarization and inhibited M2 polarization. In peripheral blood CD14+ monocytes, NEDD4L and HK3 mRNA expression correlated positively with APACHE II scores and negatively with PaO₂/FiO₂, whereas RARA mRNA expression showed the opposite associations. In conclusion, NEDD4L-mediated degradation of RARA hinders its transcriptional repression of HK3 to activate macrophage glycolysis and M1 polarization in PALI development.

articles.title: Lysosome-resident nanoreactor enables spatiotemporally controlled ferroptosis via cascade amplification of lipid peroxidation in breast cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis induced by Fenton-reaction holds great promise in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) therapy. However, its efficacy is severely constrained by limited endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) substrates and poor Fenton reaction efficiency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a strategy to initiate a heterogeneous photo-Fenton-like reaction in H2O2-rich lysosomes and design a reaction engine for amplified cascade toxic oxidative radical propagation (REACTOR), which can confine the reaction to lysosomes for light triggering and accelerate it with p-benzoquinone (DMBQ). The REACTOR nanoplatform encapsulates copper-enriched Prussian blue (CuPB) and a redox-active DMBQ within thermosensitive liposomes, enabling preferential accumulation in lysosomes. Under irradiation, REACTOR triggers lipid phase transition, exposing the co-encapsulated CuPB and DMBQ to the lysosomal H2O2 pool and initiating a highly efficient Fenton reaction that induces lysosomal membrane lipid peroxidation. Concurrently, ferrous ions released from lysosomal stores, together with CuPB-catalyzed quinone redox cycle, propagate oxidative damage to mitochondrial membranes, culminating in an explosive burst of lipid peroxides that efficiently triggers ferroptosis. REACTOR combined with irradiation significantly inhibits tumor growth, even achieving complete tumor regression and effectively suppressing metastasis in a TNBC-model. This light-activatable REACTOR transitions from a ready to a reactive state by mimicking the bombardier beetle's defense strategy, leveraging the lysosomal compartment to trigger, amplify, and sustain oxidative damage, offering a highly efficient and low-toxicity platform for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Self-augmenting procoagulant microspheres potentiate microvessel embolization and hypoxia-activated prodrug activation against hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) persists a cornerstone therapy for hypervascular tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet clinical limitations remain due to inefficient occlusion of tumor microvessels and hypoxia-induced drug resistance. Here, self-augmenting procoagulant microspheres (SPM) were developed for sustained co-delivery of thrombin (Th) and hypoxia-activated prodrug AQ4N (Th/AQ@SPM) to potentiate TACE therapy in HCC. SPM induced primary embolization by obstructing major tumor vasculature, affording vascular disruption and procoagulant factor exposure to establish a localized hypercoagulable microenvironment. Th-triggered secondary thrombosis through platelet aggregation and fibrinogen-to-fibrin conversion within residual vasculature extended occlusion to inter-microsphere spaces and distal microvessels beyond direct microsphere reach. Concurrently, hypoxia-potentiated activation of AQ4N to its cytotoxic form enabled targeted chemotherapy within the ischemic tumors. In rabbit renal and auricular artery models, Th@SPM demonstrated significant microvessel embolization through dual-phase vascular occlusion. Orthotopic VX2 liver tumor models revealed that TACE treatment with Th/AQ@SPM achieved superior tumor suppression without adverse toxic effects. Thus, Th/AQ@SPM establishes a self-augmenting embolic cascade that couples progressive microvascular occlusion with hypoxia-activated chemotherapy, providing a potent strategy to overcome key limitations of conventional TACE for HCC.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes as nanocarriers for curcumin: from fundamental research to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Curcumin has diverse pharmacological activities but poor water solubility, rapid degradation, extensive metabolism, and very low oral bioavailability limit its therapeutic use. This review evaluates mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exo; MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles per MISEV2023) as natural nanocarriers for curcumin delivery and the barriers to clinical translation. Curcumin-loaded MSC-Exo (Cur@Exos) can improve curcumin stability, sustain release, enhance target-tissue accumulation, and cross biological barriers such as the blood-brain barrier. Compared with synthetic nanocarriers, MSC-Exo may offer better biocompatibility, immune evasion, and tissue tropism, but these properties depend on source and preparation; proteomes, miRNA cargoes, and functions differ among bone marrow-, umbilical cord-, and adipose-derived MSCs. Encapsulation efficiency, batch consistency, scalability, and storage stability also remain suboptimal. Preclinical studies show Cur@Exos benefits in neurodegenerative diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, liver disease, wound healing, bone defects, and sepsis-associated kidney injury. However, findings are limited by heterogeneity in exosome sources, preparation, loading methods, and animal models; small samples and short follow-up; inconsistent dose metrics (particle number vs. protein content); and lack of standardized process and outcome criteria, reference materials, and potency assays. Long-term safety remains inadequately established: current evidence covers only short-term single or repeated dosing; ≥ 6-month repeat-dose toxicology with anti-drug antibody and complement monitoring, predictive immunogenicity screening, tumorigenicity assessment, potency-based batch release testing, and clinical efficacy data are lacking. MSC-Exo is a promising curcumin-delivery platform, but translation requires standardized manufacturing, globally harmonized quality control, improved scalability, systematic safety evaluation, well-designed multicenter trials, and a clarified international regulatory pathway.

articles.title: Parenteral drug delivery utilizing surface-eroding materials.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-acting parenteral drug delivery systems can improve therapeutic outcomes and patient adherence by achieving more consistent drug levels and reducing dosing frequency. However, many existing platforms release drugs at rates that are difficult to predict a priori and often require empirical characterization. Diffusion- and bulk degradation-based systems often exhibit burst release, nonlinear kinetics, and incomplete drug release, and can reduce encapsulated therapeutic bioactivity. Surface-eroding biomaterials offer an alternative strategy by confining degradation primarily to the material surface, enabling predictable, geometry-dependent release profiles, including the potential for zero-order drug delivery. AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes biodegradable materials exhibiting surface-eroding behavior, methods for distinguishing surface erosion from bulk degradation, and the application of surface-eroding materials in parenteral drug delivery. Literature published between 1985 and 2026 was identified through searches of PubMed, Google Scholar, and Consensus using terms related to surface erosion, polymer degradation, and controlled drug delivery, supplemented by reference-list screening and citation tracking. EXPERT OPINION: Surface-eroding materials offer opportunities for precise controlled drug release, yet translation remains limited by challenges in characterization, stability, and device manufacturing. Standardizing approaches for evaluating degradation mechanisms and advances in microscale device fabrication will be critical to defining their clinical role in parenteral drug delivery.

articles.title: Ex vivo assessment of caffeine and α-tocopherol delivery to human and porcine skin: confocal Raman spectroscopy and Franz diffusion cell/HPLC analysis.
articles.abstract: Combined topical delivery of hydrophilic and lipophilic actives requires formulation strategies capable of accommodating markedly different partitioning behaviour. Here, caffeine (CAF) and α-tocopherol (TOC) were co-formulated in phosphatidylcholine dispersions containing Tween 80, sodium deoxycholate, or DOTAP together with diethylene glycol monoethyl ether, yielding near-neutral, anionic, and cationic systems. The dispersions were characterised by light scattering and evaluated ex vivo by quantitative confocal Raman spectroscopy (CRS) in human and porcine skin and by Franz diffusion cell (FDC) analysis with HPLC quantification in porcine skin. All formulations were nanosized (approximately 75-100 nm) and retained satisfactory particle-size stability for 12 weeks at 4 °C. After 1 h of exposure, CRS revealed predominantly superficial profiles and showed model-dependent differences without a consistent ranking related to vesicle charge, with CAF more reliably resolved than TOC. After 4 h of FDC exposure, CRS showed formulation-dependent CAF distributions, with clearer differences between formulations especially in the superficial layers. HPLC confirmed transdermal CAF transport and showed the highest recovery of CAF in the dermis and receptor fluid for SPC/T80. In contrast, TOC was predominantly retained at the skin surface and within the tissue. Across both approaches, delivery of CAF and TOC was governed more by compound properties and membrane-modifier identity than by surface charge alone. These findings demonstrate the complementarity of CRS and compartment-resolved HPLC for evaluating multicomponent topical formulations.

articles.title: Thermally reversible and light-sensitive agarose hydrogels for controlled drug release.
articles.abstract: Significant work has been conducted in the development of stimuli-responsive hydrogels for triggered drug delivery, most systems still lack the ability to enable externally controlled, on-demand drug delivery over several independent cycles. This study investigates the development and performance of an agarose-based hydrogel composite integrated with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) nanoparticles for enhanced drug delivery applications. We synthesized a stable hydrogel from low-melt and low-electroendosmosis agarose and incorporated PEDOT nanoparticles to enable photothermal modulation using near-infrared (NIR) light. PEDOT nanoparticles were initially synthesized via emulsion polymerization and characterized for size distribution, zeta potential, UV-Vis absorbance, and photothermal conversion ability to confirm their successful formation. The agarose-PEDOT composite hydrogel was then prepared and evaluated comprehensively, including for photothermal performance and drug release capacity. Photothermal studies demonstrated the hydrogel's ability to absorb NIR light at 808 nm, indicating its potential for controlled, laser-triggered drug release. Drug release experiments were conducted using bovine serum albumin-fluorescein isothiocyanate (BSA-FITC) and doxorubicin (DOX) as model drugs. These studies were performed at room temperature, 37°C, and under 808-nm laser irradiation to assess the hydrogel's responsiveness to thermal and photothermal stimuli. The results showed that the agarose-PEDOT composite hydrogel exhibited excellent stability in a liquid medium, effectively retaining PEDOT nanoparticles. Additionally, the hydrogel demonstrated pulsatile release behavior for both BSA-FITC and DOX under NIR laser irradiation, providing a controllable and sustained release profile. In conclusion, this composite hydrogel offers promising potential for targeted and controlled drug delivery, particularly in applications requiring light-responsive release mechanisms.

articles.title: Safety and acceptability of placebo pellet formulations co-administered with a swallowing gel in healthy adult volunteers: a first step towards an easy-to-swallow alternative for patients with dysphagia.
articles.abstract: Swallowing oral solid dosage forms (OSDFs), such as tablets and capsules, can be challenging for individuals with dysphagia, often leading to reduced therapy adherence and unauthorized dosage form modification. Alternative oral dosage forms remain limited. Multiparticulate pellet formulations may improve swallowing acceptability due to their relatively small size and sphericity as well as offer therapeutic advantages including high drug loading, uniform gastrointestinal distribution, suitability for controlled release or taste masking if coated, and flexible dosing. This study evaluated the safety and acceptability of placebo pellets administered with swallowing gels in 34 healthy adults. Eight formulations were evaluated, varying in pellet size (500 µm versus 1000 µm), total pellet mass (250 mg versus 750 mg), and type of swallowing gel (Gloup Zero versus Gloup Forte). Swallowing safety was assessed as the primary endpoint using the Penetration Aspiration Scale (PAS) during Flexible Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing. Secondary outcomes included investigator-reported acceptability, measured using a modified Yale Pharyngeal Residue Severity Rating Scale, and participant-reported acceptability using an eight-item Visual Analogue Scale. Based on the investigator-reported scores 1) no clinically relevant airway compromise was observed in healthy adults, although one PAS 3 event occurred and 2) smaller pellet size was associated with higher pharyngeal residue scores in healthy adults. Residue was reduced after swallowing and rinsing; however, complete clearance was not consistently achieved for smaller pellet sizes. Participants reported improved swallowability with smaller pellet masses, although residue remained higher with smaller pellet sizes. While the present findings demonstrate safety and acceptability in healthy adults, dedicated clinical studies in patients with dysphagia are required to confirm the applicability of multiparticulate pellet formulations co-administered with a generically applicable swallowing gel for drug delivery.

articles.title: A versatile and simple dual-network oxime hydrogel delivery system for fine-tuning of release kinetics.
articles.abstract: Hydrogel-based drug delivery systems often require reformulation through changes in polymer composition, crosslink density, or degradable motifs to achieve different release profiles. Here, we present a dual-network oxime hydrogel platform that enables systematic tuning of protein release through adjustment of the ketoxime-to-aldoxime ratio while maintaining constant polymer composition and fabrication conditions. Hydrogels were formed by crosslinking aminooxy-functionalized 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol) with mixtures of ketone-functionalized chondroitin sulfate (CSK) and aldehyde-functionalized chondroitin sulfate (CSA), generating networks containing varying proportions of ketoxime and aldoxime linkages. All formulations rapidly formed homogeneous hydrogels under physiological conditions, exhibited clinically relevant gelation windows, and demonstrated robust self-healing behavior. Using FITC-labeled albumin as a model protein, release kinetics were systematically modulated by varying the CSK:CSA ratio, with characteristic t80 values ranging from approximately 7 to 12 days. Increasing ketoxime content prolonged protein retention, whereas increasing aldoxime content accelerated release. Equilibrium swelling-derived parameters did not correlate directly with release kinetics. In contrast, stress-relaxation measurements revealed a significant composition-dependent increase in relaxation with increasing CSA content, paralleling the trend observed in protein release. These findings support an association between oxime composition, time-dependent network relaxation, and protein release, highlighting the importance of dynamic network behavior alongside equilibrium network architecture. Importantly, hydrogels maintained high mesenchymal stem cell viability and formed localized depots following injection into porcine skin explants. Together, these results establish oxime bond composition as a simple and versatile molecular handle for fine-tuning protein release in injectable hydrogel delivery systems.

articles.title: Electrosprayed dry powder formulations of paclitaxel/carboplatin for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for about 85% of all cases. Current emerging treatment options still show limited clinical benefit, making chemotherapy an important part of NSCLC management. Although multiple clinical trials have demonstrated the efficacy of carboplatin combined with paclitaxel in patients with NSCLC, adverse reactions and safety concerns associated with traditional chemotherapy administration remain significant, highlighting the need for alternative drug delivery strategies. Pulmonary drug delivery enables direct drug deposition in the lungs with reduced systemic exposure. Dry powder formulations provide an alternative to liquid aerosol systems for pulmonary drug delivery, with electrospraying offering a flexible approach for preparing inhalable dry powder particles. In this study, electrosprayed particles based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan were developed and optimised for the pulmonary delivery of paclitaxel and carboplatin. The particles were characterised using electron microscopy, laser diffraction, and next-generation impactor, and their biological performance was evaluated in A549 and Calu-3 cells. Despite a primary particle size below 1 μm, particle aggregation led to volumetric and aerodynamic diameters within the optimal range (1-5 μm) for pulmonary deposition. The formulations showed low moisture content (<3% w/w) with good aerosol performance, achieving over 80% emitted dose and the highest effective fine particle fraction of 58.61 ± 0.83%. Both drugs were successfully encapsulated with a rapid release of 70-90% within the first 2 h. Chitosan coating increased particle adhesion and cell interaction, and cell viability studies confirmed cytotoxic effects against A549 cells over 72 h.

articles.title: Forced degradation study of etrasimod: Structural elucidation and transformation pathways of its major degradation products.
articles.abstract: Etrasimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1P1) receptor modulator and has been used for the treatment of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis. Understanding its chemical degradation behaviors is important for evaluation of intrinsic stability and degradation impurities. Herein, the degradation chemistry of solid etrasimod was systematically investigated under ICH-recommended stress conditions. Eight degradation products were detected by using reversed-phase HPLC, and three major products (DP-6, DP-4, and DP-2) was isolated and structurally elucidated by LC-MS combined with multidimensional NMR spectroscopy. DP-6 was assigned as an oxygenated lactone-containing degradation product, DP-4 as a ring-expanded dicarbonyl product, and DP-2 as an open-chain succinic acid derivative. Time-dependent transformation experiments demonstrated the conversion of DP-6 to DP-4 under oxidative conditions and DP-4 to DP-2 under alkaline conditions. These experimentally established transformation relationships, together with the structural information obtained for the major degradation products, support an interconnected degradation pathways involving oxidative transformation and subsequent alkaline hydrolysis. Overall, this study provides experimentally supported insights into the degradation chemistry and transformation relationships of etrasimod, which may facilitate the identification and monitoring of degradation impurities, the assessment of drug-substance stability, and the development of appropriate impurity control strategies during pharmaceutical development.

articles.title: Toward physiologically relevant in vitro release testing of PLGA microspheres for subcutaneous administration.
articles.abstract: Despite nearly 40 years of clinical use, PLGA microspheres (MS) still lack reliable in vitro methods to predict drug release, limiting rational development of new subcutaneous (SubQ) formulations or generics. This study investigated how components of the SubQ environment (e.g. proteins, glycosaminoglycans, and lipids) influence drug release from PLGA microspheres containing flurbiprofen or naltrexone. Four independent SubQ-relevant release media of increasing complexity were designed based on the reported SubQ tissue composition. Drug release was evaluated using the sample-and-separate method and, for the first time with PLGA microspheres, the SubCutaneous Injection Site SimulatOR (SCISSOR) containing different extracellular matrix cartridges. Medium composition affected release in a drug- and formulation-dependent manner. For flurbiprofen-loaded microspheres, differences were mainly confined to the initial burst, with limited effects on the overall release. Naltrexone release from the MS varied markedly among media and was faster and more extensive in albumin-containing media than in electrolyte- containing medium. With the SCISSOR method, flurbiprofen release from the PLGA microspheres was comparable between cartridges, reaching approximately 25% after 7 days, whereas naltrexone release from the microspheres remained below 5% after 4 days. These findings indicate that SubQ tissue components may influence PLGA microsphere performances supporting their inclusion in in vitro release methods.

articles.title: In vitro studies on the therapeutic potential of hybrid hydrogels loaded polymeric carriers - Salicylic acid and fluocinolone acetonide systems based on 3D psoriasis model.
articles.abstract: Overcoming the thickened stratum corneum is critical for effective topical psoriasis therapy. To address this, we engineered chemically cross-linked sodium alginate/poly(vinyl alcohol) hydrogels enriched with Aloe vera. These incorporate thermosensitive carriers co-loaded with salicylic acid and fluocinolone acetonide, enabling sustained drug release and enhanced penetration. Crucially, evaluation in a 3D in vitro psoriasis model confirmed the biocompatibility of the formulations and their potent anti-inflammatory activity, significantly downregulating IL-6, DEFB4, elafin, S100A7, and S100A12. Using this advanced 3D model provides critical insights into the formulation's mechanism of action, highlighting its potential for targeted, safe psoriasis management.

articles.title: A multimodal anticancer strategy based on exosome-coated prussian blue nanocarriers for melanoma treatment.
articles.abstract: Overcoming multidrug resistance and tumor recurrence in melanoma requires multimodal therapeutic strategies that surpass the limitations of monotherapy. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanoplatform, HMPB@EX-DOX, designed to combine chemotherapy, photothermal therapy (PTT), and iron-mediated oxidative stress to potentially contribute to ferroptosis-like cell death. The platform is based on hollow mesoporous Prussian blue nanocubes (HMPB), which provide a high specific surface area for doxorubicin (DOX) loading. It is further functionalized with mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-EX) to enhance biocompatibility and promote tumor accumulation. Under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the system induced photothermal heating, chemotherapeutic drug release, and intracellular ROS generation, collectively enhancing oxidative stress in melanoma cells. In vitro clonogenic assays demonstrated that the combined treatment significantly suppressed colony formation to 10.2 ± 1.5%, outperforming single- or dual-modality groups (n = 3, p < 0.001). The biomimetic nanoplatform HMPB@EX-DOX exhibited significant ROS generation in vitro in B16F0 cells, which was enhanced under NIR irradiation. Cellular fluorescence analysis suggested a greater DOX-associated signal in B16F0 cells for HMPB@EX-DOX than for HMPB-DOX. In vivo evaluation in B16F0 melanoma-bearing mice demonstrated significant inhibition of tumor growth. The prepared HMPB@EX-DOX platform exhibited tumor accumulation and photothermal conversion at the tumor site under NIR irradiation. The developed platform was also capable of preclinical MR imaging and showed potential for in vivo contrast enhancement, while histopathological analysis suggested acceptable short-term biosafety of the prepared platform under the tested conditions. Overall, HMPB@EX-DOX represents a promising biomimetic nanoplatform for combined melanoma therapy, offering a useful foundation for future nanomedicine development.

articles.title: Corni Fructus water extract relieves depressive behaviors by reducing oxidative stress and neuroinflammation as well as modulating gut microbiota.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Depression is a global public health concern with limited therapies. Traditional Chinese medicines are attractive for safety and multi-target actions. Corni Fructus water extract (CFWE) is a candidate, but its mechanisms and the main active ingredients remain unclear. METHODS: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established and given CFWE intervention. Depressive-like behaviors were evaluated by sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and open field test (OFT). Hippocampal histopathology was examined using H&E staining. Inflammatory and oxidative stress-related factors in the hippocampus and serum were detected using ELISA kits. RT-qPCR and Western blot measured Nrf2/HO-1 and IκBα/NF-κB pathway components. Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing and GC-MS. LC-MS determined the major chemical constituents of CFWE. RESULTS: CFWE significantly alleviated CUMS-induced depressive-like phenotypes, including preserved body weight, reduced immobility time in TST, increased sucrose preference, and greater central distance in OFT (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). It also increased neuronal survival in hippocampal CA1/CA3 (P < 0.01), lowered pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and MDA (P < 0.05) in serum and hippocampus, and elevated CAT and SOD activities dose-dependently (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, CFWE upregulated Nrf2, HO-1, and IκBα expression, while downregulating phosphorylated NF-κB p65 expression (P < 0.05). It also restored gut microbial diversity (P < 0.05), promoted beneficial taxa (Muribaculaceae and Lactobacillus), enhanced SCFAs production, and elevated peripheral peptide YY (PYY). LC-MS analysis revealed that the main active constituents in CFWE were terpenoid glycosides, flavonoid glycosides, and organic oxygen compounds. CONCLUSION: The antidepressant-like effects of CFWE might involve activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway, suppression of the IκBα/NF-κB inflammatory response, and modulation of gut microbiota composition and SCFA metabolism, while PYY might serve as a candidate mediator in gut-brain communication.

articles.title: Adolescent intermittent ethanol exposure alters responsiveness to acute low dose ethanol challenge and functional connectivity in adult male rats.
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental period characterized by a unique pattern of sensitivity to ethanol. Preclinical research revealed that adolescent rats are less sensitive than adults to a number of adverse effects of ethanol, while adolescent intermittent ethanol (AIE) exposure preserves an adolescent-typical phenotype of ethanol responsiveness. The present study used transgenic Fos-LacZ male rats to test the long-term effects of AIE on sensitivity to the socially impairing effects of ethanol and accompanying patterns of neuronal activation in brain regions implicated in social interaction. Experimental subjects were exposed to 4 g/kg ethanol or water given intragastrically every other day for a total of 11 exposures during postnatal days (P) 25-45. On P70, animals were challenged with ethanol (0 or 0.75 g/kg) and assessed in a modified social interaction test. While water-exposed controls demonstrated significant ethanol-induced decreases of social investigation and social preference, indicative of socially suppressing effects of ethanol, AIE-exposed subjects were insensitive to this effect. AIE enhanced the positive relationships between social investigation and neuronal activation in salience network-associated regions, with acute ethanol eliminating these relationships. Graph-based functional connectivity analyses revealed marked AIE-associated changes in overall network organization and hub region involvement, with acute ethanol disrupting network connectivity to a much greater extent in AIE-exposed subjects than in water controls. These data suggest that AIE induces long-lasting reorganization of the social brain network and enhanced sensitivity to functional circuit disruption.
